sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cell-based functionality test confirmed the 3HA–LGR4–FLAG construct retains receptor function (L2, PMC5602029).
sites.rationale: The paper explicitly places the 3HA tag 'downstream [of the] signaling peptide', which by the topology landmarks ends at residue 24; the tag therefore sits between residue 24 (A) and residue 25 (A), the first residue of the 518-residue extracellular domain (span 25–542). Python confirmed residue 24 = A and residue 25 = A. The site is 518 residues from TM1 (residue 543), far exceeding the ≥3-residue minimum. Functional validation is provided by the cell-based assay in L2, and endogenous-locus tolerance is confirmed by the knock-in in L3. Full-length human LGR4 was expressed as a membrane-anchored receptor with a 3HA tag inserted immediately downstream of the signal peptide (residues 1–24) and a FLAG tag at the intracellular C-terminus, in the pK-myc backbone (L1). The same 3HA tag was knocked into the endogenous mouse Lgr4 locus using a construct with homology arms flanking the tag sequence (L3). A cell-based functionality test of the tagged receptor was performed (L2).

sources.claim: The 3HA–LGR4–FLAG construct encoding human LGR4 including N-terminal insertion of the 3HA tag (downstream signaling peptide) and with the FLAG tag at its C-terminus was generated in the pK-myc backbone (Valenta et al. 2006 ) using human LGR4 cDNA ( NM_018490 ; purchased from OriGene) and a site-directed mutagenesis kit (Stratagene).

literature_notes: L4 and L5 report LgBiT and GFP fused to the C-terminus of full-length LGR4. The topology landmarks place the C-terminus (residues 805–951) in the intracellular compartment; these fusions are therefore not extracellular surface sites and are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for LGR4.

literature_other_positions.note: FLAG tag fused to the C-terminus of full-length LGR4; topology landmarks place residues 805–951 in the intracellular compartment.
